Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

relevant adjective

also be relevant, pertinent, to the point, irrelevant, that’s beside the point, have nothing to do with

classical

Cic. Div. 2.98: sī ad rem pertinet (Lewis & Short, s.v. pertineō)
Cic. Fam. 13.13: sī quid hoc ad rem pertinet
M-O s.v. relevant

ad rem pertinēre

phrase: pertineō, pertinēre, with ad rem

to be relevant, bear on the matter

The usual way; with another noun, ad hanc quaestiōnem pertinet, “it’s relevant to this question”.

Other words

  • nihil ad rem — irrelevant, beside the point

    phrase, with or without pertinet · also used · classical · Cic. Caecin. 58: nihil ad rem pertinet (Lewis & Short, s.v. pertineō); Cic. Fin. 1.5: nihil ad Epicūrum

    Often without the verb: Nihil ad rem!, “That’s beside the point!”

  • aliēnus (ab) — foreign to, out of place in, irrelevant to

    adjective, with ab + ablative or the dative · also used · classical · M-O s.v. relevant

    Literally “belonging to another”: what does not belong to the matter in hand.

Examples

  • cum virtūtibus tum etiam fortūnā, sī quid hoc ad rem pertinet

    in his virtues and also in his fortune, if this is relevant at allCic. Fam. 13.13 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nihil ad rem! Respondē ad id quod rogāvī.

    That’s beside the point! Answer what I asked.composed

See also issue, important.

SourcesLewis & Short: pertineo · Lewis & Short: alienus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. relevant.

Cicero quoted as Lewis & Short quotes him.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
